## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 79, titled *Sokāvāsa*, is a disciplinary rule for Buddhist nuns preserved in the *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who ordains a trainee nun (*sikkhamānā*) who socializes inappropriately and is difficult to live with commits an offence requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records parallels across numerous early Buddhist Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. In Pali, these comprise the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 79) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pc 79) [SuttaCentral]. Parallels in other lineages include the Dharmaguptaka (*Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 135* and *lzh-dg-bi-pm-pc135*), the Sarvāstivāda (*Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc118*, *lzh-sarv-bi-pm-dh-pc119*, and *lzh-sarv-bi-pm-pc118*), and the Mūlasarvāstivāda tradition preserved in both Chinese (*Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 118*, *lzh-mu-bi-pm-pc118*) and Tibetan (*xct-mu-bi-vb-pc88*, *xct-mu-bi-pm-pc88*, *xct-mu-bi-vb-pc89*, *xct-mu-bi-pm-pc89*) [SuttaCentral].
